content:
Let \(x=\angle A\), \(y=\angle B\), \(z=\angle C\).  
Given \(y=\frac52x\), so
\[
z=180-x-\frac52x=180-\frac72x.
\]
Since \(\angle A\) is smallest and \(\angle B\) largest:
\[
x\le z\le y.
\]

From \(x\le z\):
\[
x\le 180-\frac72x \implies \frac92x\le 180 \implies x\le 40.
\]
From \(z\le y\):
\[
180-\frac72x\le \frac52x \implies 180\le 6x \implies x\ge 30.
\]
Thus \(30\le x\le 40\), and
\[
y=\frac52x \implies 75^\circ\le y\le 100^\circ.
\]
So minimum \(\angle B=75^\circ\), maximum \(\angle B=100^\circ\). Their sum is
\[
75+100=175.
\]

\[
\boxed{175}
\]
